sources.citation: Theil Endresen, Rolf. 1992. La phonologie de la langue nizaa (nizaà). Nordic Journal of African Studies 1(1): 28-52.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full segmental + tonal phonology (sect. 1 syllable, 2 vowels, 3 consonants, 5 'La tonologie': three levels H/M/B, nine lexical tones incl. contours HM HB MH MB BH BHM, downstep, floating H, tone transport). No word for accent/stress/prominence anywhere in the publisher's scanned text layer (checked both layout and raw extracted text; scanned is garbled because the scan is 2-up, so a missed line is possible but unlikely).

sources.citation: Kjelsvik, Bjørghild. 2002. Verb chains in Nizaa. MA (cand.philol.) thesis, University of Oslo. 189 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 2.1 Phonology (pp. 9-13): syllable types CV/CVV/CVC, 5+10+7 vowels, 61 onset / 10 coda consonants, coda weakening, 2.1.5 Tones: 'three tone levels, high (H), mid (M) and low (L).. combined to complex tones', downstep, tone transport. Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Pepper, Steve. 2020. The typology and semantics of binominal lexemes: Noun-noun compounds and their functional equivalents. PhD dissertation, University of Oslo. 540 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nizaa only as a compounding case study (1.1.2, p. 5; based on Theil's unpublished 1980s field notes); mentions a definite/specific low tone suffix; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pepper, Steve. 2016. Windmills, Nizaa and the typology of binominal compounds. In Körtvélyessy, Štekauer & Valera (eds.), Word-formation across languages, 281-310. Cambridge Scholars Publishing.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only other published Nizaa description with a language sketch; open file held by NVA (hdl 10852/55588 / 11250/3229252) but download API refused our network.

sources.citation: Kjelsvik, Bjørghild. 2008. Emergent speech genres of teaching and learning interaction. Communities of practice in Cameroonian schools and villages. PhD dissertation, University of Oslo (Acta Humaniora). 419 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 4.4.1 Language description (pp. 111-113) and 4.4.2 Tones (pp. 112-114): 'a rich tonology, with three distinctive tonelevels and a number of tone combinations used as lexical tones.. tones are regularily transported', refers to Endresen 1992 for the full system. The only 'accent language' remark (p. 173) concerns Fulfulde, not Nizaa. No Nizaa stress statement.
